title: Sling Load per Leg
subtitle: Angle-adjusted tension in each leg of a multi-leg sling
formula_display: Load per leg = (Total load ÷ Legs) ÷ cos(θ/2)

inputs.label: Included angle between legs at the hook
inputs.help: 0° = legs vertical (parallel) — no angle penalty. 60° = each leg has 30° from vertical. Above 60° gets dangerous fast.

bands.note: High tension — check sling WLL carefully
DO NOT exceed 120° included angle per ASME B30.9

notes: Load per leg increases rapidly with angle. At 120° included angle, each leg carries roughly the full load. Always compare the calculated leg load to the sling's Working Load Limit (WLL) for the actual hitch used (vertical, choker, or basket).

citations.ref: Slings — load calculations and angle factors
